projects.title: Industrial fuel management system
projects.summary: A fuel dispensing and transaction-management architecture that turns pulses from a flow meter into vehicle-linked transactions, printed receipts and ERP records.
projects.contribution: Engineering of the edge, application and integration layers: pulse acquisition, transaction logic, operator PWA, receipt printing and ERP synchronisation.
projects.challenge: Every litre dispensed has to become an accurate, attributable record — linked to a vehicle, driver and company — even when the site's uplink is down, and without double-counting when it comes back.
approach: Pulse inputs from the meter's pulser are counted on an industrial Raspberry Pi controller and converted to volume at the edge, so measurement never depends on the network.
Node-RED flows own the transaction lifecycle: open ticket, live volume, close ticket, persist locally.
An offline-first PWA gives the operator vehicle and driver registration, live volume and ticket closing on a phone or tablet.
Closed transactions print as thermal receipts on site and queue for synchronisation to the ERP, with retries and duplicate prevention.
Transaction history and spreadsheet exports come from the same records, so the printed receipt, the local log and the ERP agree.

projects.title: Security checkpoint and visitor management
projects.summary: An offline-capable checkpoint PWA for registering visitors and vehicles, tracking check-in and check-out, and synchronising every movement to an ERP backend.
projects.contribution: Design and implementation of the checkpoint application, its offline synchronisation and the backend integration.
projects.challenge: Gate staff need a fast, simple tool that keeps working when the connection drops, while the backend still needs a complete, traceable record of who and what entered and left — and from which device.
approach: A mobile-first PWA captures visitor and vehicle registrations, check-in and check-out at the gate.
Transactions are stored locally first and synchronised through REST APIs, with per-record sync state so nothing is silently lost.
Each device is identified, so every record shows where it was captured.
Time-on-site and visitor status are derived from the transaction log rather than typed in.
The backend is a Frappe / ERPNext integration, so checkpoint data sits alongside the organisation's other operational records.

projects.title: Industrial monitoring and automation
projects.summary: PLC-based equipment telemetry, threshold logic and alarms, published over MQTT and WebSockets into historical trends and remote operator dashboards.
projects.contribution: Edge logic, protocol integration, data pipeline and dashboards for remote visibility of physical processes.
projects.challenge: Physical equipment speaks in registers, inputs and pulses. Operators and managers need states, alarms and trends — locally when the network is down and remotely when it is up.
approach: Industrial Raspberry Pi PLCs read digital and analog inputs and poll equipment over Modbus.
Node-RED handles register decoding (signed and unsigned, 16- and 32-bit), threshold evaluation, process timers and machine-state transitions.
Processing stays local during connectivity interruptions; services recover automatically after a reboot.
Readings and events publish over MQTT and WebSockets to InfluxDB for history and to dashboards for live view.
Grafana and custom operator screens show equipment state, alarms, historical trends and network connectivity.

architecture.detail: Live state, trends and alarm views.

architecture.label: Operator action
architecture.detail: Respond to alarms and process states.

projects.title: Fleet intelligence and telematics platform
projects.summary: GPS telematics turned into operational intelligence: live maps, trip history and replay, geofences, driver behaviour, alerts and scheduled reports for fleet operations.
projects.contribution: Engineering contribution to a fleet-operations platform: telematics integration, event processing, alerting and reporting. Not a claim of sole ownership of every product feature.
projects.challenge: Raw GPS and device events are noisy and voluminous. Dispatchers and operations teams need the few events that matter, on a live map, with a history they can trust.
approach: Teltonika telematics devices report position and events; fleet data is handled through GpsGate.
Events are filtered and classified — geofence crossings, harsh braking and acceleration, vehicle state — before they reach a person.
Live maps, trip history and route replay give dispatch a shared operational picture.
Alert rules and scheduled reports deliver driver-behaviour and fleet summaries without manual collection.
Dispatch, work-order and maintenance-planning workflows are designed to build on the same vehicle data.

architecture.detail: GPS position, ignition and driving events.

architecture.label: Dispatch / response
architecture.detail: Act on alerts and assign work.

projects.title: Intelligent LED matrix control
projects.summary: Microcontroller-driven HUB75 RGB LED matrices that display live process values, text and alarm states commanded over MQTT.
projects.contribution: Display firmware and the MQTT command interface that lets industrial data drive physical signage.
projects.challenge: Operators on the ground need to read a process value or a warning from a distance, in daylight, and the display has to follow live data without anyone touching it.
approach: RP2040 (Pimoroni Interstate75 / Pico W) and ESP32-S3 boards drive HUB75 P4 64×32 RGB panels, including four-panel 2×2 layouts.
MicroPython firmware handles multi-panel matrix mapping, centring, brightness and rendering.
Node-RED publishes values and commands over MQTT; the display subscribes and renders text, flow rates and status.
Configurable high/low thresholds change colours, and alarm modes flash for warning conditions.
Background and text colours are configurable remotely over the same command channel.

architecture.detail: MicroPython render loop, thresholds, alarm modes.

projects.title: AI agent engineering laboratory
projects.summary: A working multi-agent software-development setup with coordinated technical roles and human approval gates, alongside local LLM experiments and automation workflows.
projects.contribution: Design and operation of the agent roles, instructions, delegation workflow and approval rules; integration of the tools. The models themselves are third-party.
projects.challenge: AI assistance is useful in engineering only when it is structured: clear roles, persistent context, reviewable output, and hard limits on what an agent may change without a human.
approach: Specialised agents for frontend, backend, IoT, DevOps, security review and coordination, each with a written role definition (AGENTS.md-style instructions).
Work is delegated as tracked tasks with plans, reviews and explicit human approval before anything is merged, deployed or touches a device.
Persistent agent memory and project context carry decisions between sessions.
Local models run through Ollama for experiments, tool calling and model comparison; hosted models are selected per task with fallbacks.
n8n and scripted workflows are used for information collection, documentation and scheduled monitoring.

architecture.detail: Sets objectives and approves sensitive actions.

architecture.detail: Selected per task; local via Ollama.

architecture.label: Review and approval gate
architecture.detail: Nothing reaches production without a human.

projects.title: Custom business and ERP solutions
projects.summary: Frappe / ERPNext applications, DocTypes, print formats and integrations that connect operational field systems to business processes.
projects.contribution: Custom app development, print-format design, integrations and site deployment on Frappe / ERPNext.
projects.challenge: Field systems produce transactions; the business runs on quotations, invoices, assets and records. The two have to meet in one system without fighting the ERP framework.
approach: Custom Frappe apps and DocTypes model operational records the standard ERP does not cover.
Jinja print formats produce branded quotations, invoices and operational documents.
REST APIs and web forms receive data from external PWAs and edge systems, with server-side business rules.
Payroll and Namibian tax-related configuration are handled inside ERPNext rather than in side spreadsheets.
Sites run on self-hosted ERPNext on Linux / nginx with HTTPS.

architecture.label: Business users
architecture.detail: Billing, payroll, asset and record management.

projects.title: Real-time monitoring and dashboard interfaces
projects.summary: Grafana and custom web dashboards that present live telemetry, alarms, system status and history in timezone-correct, filterable, exportable views.
projects.contribution: Dashboard design and implementation, live data plumbing and reporting views.
projects.challenge: Telemetry is only useful if an operator can read it at a glance, find the event that matters and export what a manager asks for — with timestamps in local time.
approach: Grafana over InfluxDB for time-series trends and alarm panels.
Custom HTML/CSS/JavaScript dashboards fed over WebSockets and MQTT for live tables and status views.
Sorting, filtering and historical event views on the same data the live screen uses.
Timezone-aware display (Africa/Windhoek) and downloadable reports.
Dense, dark, high-contrast layouts designed for control-room use.
